title: Wild sign coach John Hynes to multiyear contract extension
content:
The Minnesota Wild have signed coach John Hynes to a multiyear extension, the team announced Tuesday.

Hynes, 51, was entering the final year of his current contract and his third full season with the Wild. He’s led the team to a 125-78-24 regular-season record and two playoff appearances (7-10). The years will be tacked onto his current deal.

Last season under Hynes, Minnesota made its first appearance in the second round in a decade before losing to the Presidents’ Trophy-winning Colorado Avalanche in five games. It didn’t end well, with a no-show in Game 4 and a blown three-goal lead in Game 5, but president of hockey operations and general manager Bill Guerin was quick to give Hynes a vote of confidence after the season in his exit interview press conference.

Guerin said Hynes’ messaging, details and prep work are “lights out” and indicated that his entire staff would return.

“John did a great job this year,” Guerin said. “I’m a big believer in John and what he does and how he operates. I see it firsthand. Not just the amount of work that goes into it, because anybody can sit at a desk and a computer for hours upon time and say they did a lot of work. To me, that’s fine. It’s the detail of which he does it in. If you could have seen the detail of the work and the time that these guys put in in between Game 2 and 3, to make those adjustments, to deliver the message to the team.

“That’s why I believe in John. It’s because of the detail in which he goes through and the messaging. We sit in his office quite a few times a year and talk about messaging to the players, to the power play, to the penalty kill, to the players as a whole — what’s the message? How are they going to grasp it the best? I really think that’s one of the things that separates John from other coaches is the time that he puts into the messaging. It’s not just, ‘This is what I say. I’m cramming it down your throat. Do it.’ He gives them the reason why — why we’re going to do this, why we’re going to have success doing it. He shows it to them, goes through it with them time and time again, and I think when the guys are on and they carry it out, it’s a Game 3. And when they’re not as focused as they need to be or on, it’s a Game 4.”

This Wild team had expectations as high as they’ve ever been, especially after their mid-December trade for Quinn Hughes.

Hynes did not have top shutdown center Joel Eriksson Ek or defenseman Jonas Brodin for the Colorado series, which definitely hurt. The challenge for Hynes is to get the Wild over this next hump during what Guerin believes is their Stanley Cup window. Hynes is just 11-25 in six career postseason appearances, with one series victory.

Hynes took over for Dean Evason in November of 2023. The team missed the playoffs that season, not able to fully recover after a tough start. The Wild made the postseason in Hynes’ first full season, thanks to Eriksson Ek’s goal in the final minute of regulation of the season finale. They played a competitive first-round series against the Vegas Golden Knights but lost in six games.

Minnesota beat the Dallas Stars in six games in the first round last season, the team’s first playoff series win since 2015. Hynes then made some debatable decisions in the second round, including starting Filip Gustavsson in Game 2. Gustavsson hadn’t played in three weeks and was, as the team revealed after the season, playing through a hip issue that required surgery. The Wild’s dominant Game 3 win against the Avalanche served as a blueprint, but they did not follow that in Game 4, a turning point in the series.

“I’ve known Hynsie since I was 17. So, kind of weird. But it was really nice to play for him,” said veteran Nick Foligno. “Honestly, I really enjoyed him. I thought he was prepared. I think he had us ready to go every game. I really enjoyed the coaching staff. I mean, it’s a small sample size, but I thought when it came down to it, I think every guy felt extremely prepared for what was to come. They did their work. They gave us a great game plan, so I appreciate all the work they did and really enjoyed playing for Hynsie and the coaching staff and getting to know them. So, yeah, I hope they continue to do their thing.”
